body_ar:
سبب تسمية الكلالة بهذه التسمية.
السؤال: لماذا سمي ميراث الكلالة بهذا الاسم؟ الجواب: أن الكلالة من (كلَّ) بمعنى تعب، والإنسان الذي ليس له أصل ولا فرع كأنه قد تعب من الحياة فانقطع وحده، ويقال: كلَّ الفرس إذا جرى حتى انقطع، وكلَّ السيف إذا لم يقطع، وكلَّ الإنسان بمعنى: تعب من سيره، فمن هنا جاء اشتقاق الكلالة.......
معنى الأذن في قوله تعالى: (ويقولون هو أذن قل أذن خير لكم):
السؤال: قال تعالى: وَيَقُولُونَ هُوَ أُذُنٌ قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ [التوبة:61] ، هل (أذن) هنا بمعنى: الاستماع؟.
الجواب: لا؛ لأن الآية قرئت بقراءتين سبعيتين: (قُلْ أُذْنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ) بالإسكان، وقرئت: (قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ)[التوبة:61]، بالضم، والمعنى في كلتيهما أي: موصل، فالأذن عند العرب هو المحقن الذي يحقن به اللبن في وعاء اللبن، والمقصود به: ما يبلغ، فقد كان المنافقون إذا طلب منهم تعظيم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقولون: ما هو إلا أذن، أي: مبلغ عن الله فقط، فكأنه بمثابة المحقن الذي يحقن فيه اللبن، ثم لا يكون له فائدة بعد ذلك، فرد الله عليهم هذا القول بقوله: قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَيُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ [التوبة:61]...
body_en:
## Why kalālah is called by this name

**Question:** Why is the inheritance of kalālah called by this name?

**Answer:** kalālah is from kalla, meaning to grow weary. A person who has neither ascendant nor descendant is as though he had grown weary of life and so was cut off alone. One says: the horse kalla, when it runs until it gives out; and the sword kalla, when it no longer cuts; and the man kalla, meaning that he grew weary from his journeying. From here comes the derivation of kalālah……

## The meaning of "ear" in His words, exalted is He: {And they say, "He is an ear." Say: "An ear of good for you"}

**Question:** God, exalted is He, said: {And they say, "He is an ear." Say: "An ear of good for you"} (Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:61). Does "ear" here mean listening?

**Answer:** No — because the verse has been read with two of the seven canonical readings (qirāʾāt): "Say: an ear (udhn) of good for you", with the vowelless letter; and it has been read "Say: an ear (udhun) of good for you" (Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:61), with the ḍammah. The meaning in both is: one who conveys.

For "the ear" among the Arabs is the funnel through which milk is poured into the milk vessel, and what is meant by it is that which conveys. When the hypocrites were asked to honour the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would say: "He is nothing but an ear" — that is, one who merely conveys from God — as though he were in the position of the funnel into which the milk is poured, and which then has no further use after that. So God answered this saying of theirs with His words: {Say: an ear of good for you. He believes in God, and has faith in the believers, and is a mercy to those of you who believe} (Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:61)…

flags.note: TITLE/BODY MISMATCH, style guide section 11 — a second confirmed instance after record 397. The title places this as the fourteenth and final instalment of the creed series on the divine names and attributes. The body contains nothing of the kind: it is two question-and-answer exchanges, one on the etymology of kalālah in the law of inheritance and one on the word 'ear' at Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:61. Neither touches the names or the attributes. The most likely explanation is that this is the question-and-answer tail of a session in the series, filed under the session's title; that is a guess and is not acted on. Both title and body are translated faithfully and the record is flagged rather than repaired. It must not be displayed as the conclusion of the series.

flags.context: فالأذن عند العرب هو المحقن الذي يحقن به اللبن في وعاء اللبن
options: the funnel through which milk is poured
the vessel into which milk is poured
flags.note: A pastoral implement whose exact form is not settled in the dictionaries, and the choice changes the force of the hypocrites' insult — a funnel merely passes the milk on, while a vessel holds it. The Sheikh's own gloss ('what is meant by it is that which conveys', and 'then has no further use after that') supports the passing-on sense, so the first option is used. A Mauritanian reader may know the object precisely; the Sheikh's office should confirm.

flags.context: the two readings of أذن at Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:61
options: two of the seven canonical readings
flags.note: The Sheikh names neither reader. No attribution is supplied in the English, and the difference between the two readings is one of vowelling only, which does not survive into English at all — hence the Arabic forms are retained in brackets so the reader can see what is at issue.
